Hi Pavithra, thanks for the patch, however it needs some rework as noted inline.
Please trim the trailing `\`.
Done
Please trim the trailing whitespace
Done
What about errors? What if the sensor ID provided doesn't exist?
Acknowledged

None of this is testing the length of the buffer before the casts to the struct types.

Please use the msgbuf APIs for spatial memory safety and endianness correctness.
Acknowledged my bad, I have made changes by using msgbuf API for spatial memory safety and endianness correctness.

This is starting to get a bit unmaintainable. Can we please define proper extraction functions for the data structure of interest? What are we even skipping here?

Further this, the assignment impedes optimisation as despite the value being an integer constant expression, assignment into the variable means that it's not propagated as such (this is why constants tend to be defined as macros in C).
acknowledged, I have made changes to define proper extraction functions.

See my comment here:

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/78458/comment/076ed358_da5a534e/
This still needs to be addressed.
Done
Done
Is `record_handle` allowed to be `NULL`? What behaviour occurs? This needs to be documented.
Acknowledged

Is it possible for this function to fail? If so, the errors need to be documented.

(you're taking pointers for arguments, so presumably this might want to error out if they're `NULL`, or if there's no such sensor ID).
Acknowledged
Isn't this rather provided by the `record_handle` out-parameter? I expect we want to return 0 on success.
yes, I have updated the doxygen as if success return is the out-param.
`0` seems strange. I think `-ENOENT` is preferable here.
Done
`return -ENOENT`?
Done

This mentions nothing about the actual return value now though 😞. The documentation is meant to be a specification that the function implements, and if this is the case, function could effectively return any value on success aside from `-EINVAL` and `-ENOENT`, which is not a very nice thing for callers to then have to handle. This should say:

> @return 0 on success, with the record handle of the deleted sensor PDR stored in `record_handle` if `record_handle` is non-NULL. Otherwise, returns -EINVAL ...
Acknowledged
`-ENOENT`?
Done
This is better, thanks. However, the sentence is now broken (and the wrapping is a bit funky). Can you please fix both (make complete sentences, with sensible line wrapping at the line limit)?
Acknowledged
Needs to be rebased to fix up the conflict in the changelog.
Done
